title: Geometric compatibility of specified normalized reduction tensor comparisons
statement: Fix ell,E, schemes T and Tprime on which ell is invertible, and g:Tprime to T. Fix coefficient-tower realizations D,Dprime, normalized reductions r,rprime and any specified monoidal reduction towers M,Mprime satisfying their strict generator, signed-total summand and derived-counit normalizations. There exists a SpReductionPullbackTower p for these given reductions and a SpReductionPullbackCoherence for these same M,Mprime and p. Thus the coefficient, evaluation, generator and derived-counit normalizations, and the tensor and unit geometric comparison squares, hold for already specified endpoint monoidal towers. This theorem constructs no endpoint monoidal tower.

source.place: Tags 03EL (sites-modules.tex), 07A4, 0G7E and 0D6D; blueprint/latest integral direct-image proof (3).

proof.text: Pull back integral coefficients from the point and the constant quotient coefficients. Their canonical identifications fix constant sections and commute with every actual completion projection. On the sequence site take the geometric inverse image, whose product-site Kan-extension generators are the original pulled-back sections. This gives the integral, level and sequence algebraic module inverse images and their exactness.

The two composite ringed inverse images agree on module generators q tensor a; their ring maps agree by the projection equations. The normalized composition and geometric 2-isomorphism comparisons give ordinary and derived comparison nu on whole systems. K-flat pullback computations identify its representative square with the displayed counit square. Evaluation on Kan generators proves the evaluation-section normalization.

For the two prescribed monoidal towers, take the normalized inverse-image tensor models. The composition comparison tensor and unit diagrams supply the required equations. On flat-term K-flat pairs they use exactly the balancing map fixed by the towers summand and derived squares. Two-variable localization uniqueness identifies them with the prescribed mu maps on all derived systems. No faithfulness of level evaluation is used.

    (hl : ∀ x : T, IsUnit (l : T.residueField x))
    (D : SpCoefficientTowersAbelian l E T) (r : SpReductionTower l E T D)
    (M : SpReductionMonoidalTower l E T D r)
    {T' : Scheme.{u}} (hl' : ∀ x : T', IsUnit (l : T'.residueField x)) (g : T' ⟶ T)
    (D' : SpCoefficientTowersAbelian l E T') (r' : SpReductionTower l E T' D')
    (M' : SpReductionMonoidalTower l E T' D' r') :
    ∃ p : SpReductionPullbackTower l E T D r g D' r',
      Nonempty (SpReductionPullbackCoherence l E T D r M g D' r' M' p)
